\altyazi{fig:study_overview}{\textbf{Study overview as one scene.} (a) Trained models: the two-by-two design, one slice per run, beside the R32 bridge; (b) Reference panels, decks of robust CNNs, sliced into (c) their PGD-10 matrices; (d) Registered before measurement gives the test families; (e) Exact split and contrasts factors each log rate. Depth runs from inputs (back) to the derived split (front).}  % 59 words
\altyazi{fig:design_recipe}{\textbf{Architecture-by-initialization design as a card cabinet.} On CIFAR-10 the drawer rows ViT-Tiny and ResNet-18 cross the columns scratch (random init.) and ImageNet init.; each drawer gives its clean stage (epochs, learning rate) and seeds, one index card per run. The R32 bridge drawer keeps its own recipe; the sign on top is the AT recipe of the four cells.}  % 59 words
\altyazi{fig:decomposition_schematic}{\textbf{Decomposition used throughout, in three tiers.} Top to bottom, the arrows per pair (i, j), panel mean and R minus V mark three steps: the log transfer rate splits exactly into vulnerability, similarity and half a directional residual; panel averages give $\sigma$ and $\rho$; the source gap G splits into symmetric and directional parts. Tiers recede with the aggregation level.}  % 60 words
\altyazi{fig:panel_members}{\textbf{Reference panel members as books on two shelves.} The front shelf, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, gives each RobustBench identifier its role in the C10 and C100 columns and marks ResNet-18 variants in the R18 column. The back shelf, ImageNetV2, holds the CNN panel and the secondary XCiT-S12, then the transformer pairs and the unpaired ViT-B of Mo et al.}  % 58 words
\altyazi{fig:registry_map}{\textbf{Registered tests and decision rules as a staircase.} Each step is one family, numbered in registration order and set behind the previous one; rows give test and quantity, place the predicted size (diamond) and falsification threshold (circle) on a number line with the $\pm$0.1 band, and state the falsifying rule. Holm correction is per family; ImageNetV2 rows are descriptive.}  % 59 words
\altyazi{fig:prereg_chain}{\textbf{Pre-registration chain as a time shelf.} Seen beforehand lists the data looked at before registration; Main registration: B2-B6 and Supplement: B8-B10, the addendum of the text, give each block's models, images and cells. Cards recede in time; arrows carry the freeze dates (October 2026), commits and registration digest prefix; the strip Added after the fact names two post hoc analyses.}  % 60 words
\altyazi{fig:source_gap_split}{\textbf{Source gap split into symmetric and directional parts, one slab per data set.} Per seed pair on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 and per same-recipe pair on ImageNetV2 (descriptive): olive symmetric part, lavender-grey directional part, diamond total G. Strips lie in the slab plane; the printed G and share q carry the values. A dashed part narrows the gap.}  % 57 words
\altyazi{fig:similarity_matrix}{\textbf{Pairwise symmetric similarity on three plinths.} $\log\simt$ (split-half) for all models on CIFAR-10 (1), CIFAR-100 (2) and ImageNetV2 (3), in frozen group order; cell colour is one of five joint quintile bins, the dark diagonal undefined. Dark frames mark the groups; no height carries a value. Scratch-trained ViT-Tiny seeds form a block dissimilar to the CNN panel.}  % 58 words
\altyazi{fig:cells_interaction}{\textbf{Two-by-two cells on CIFAR-10 as a three-floor tower.} Floors Panel similarity $\sigma$, Direction $\rho$ and Vulnerability $\omega$ share the posts at scratch and ImageNet; lines join cell means (split-half, log scale), open marks are runs, diamonds the R32 bridge. $\sigma$ prints $\Asig{scr}$ (H1) and $\Isig$ (H2); $\rho$ carries the $\pm$0.10 band. Values are positions on each floor.}  % 58 words
\altyazi{fig:attack_side}{\textbf{Transfer by attack, per source, on an abacus.} Each wire is one source; beads sit at its panel-mean log transfer L(m) under PGD-10 (circle), momentum PGD (square) and, for ViT sources, TGR (triangle). Filled beads are the attacks chosen by cross-fitted selection; TGR is never chosen. The value is the bead's position on the beam scale.}  % 56 words
\altyazi{fig:gradient_alignment}{\textbf{Input-gradient alignment against similarity on a two-step stand.} Cosine c between input gradients on clean images against $\log\simt$ for every model pair on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNetV2; back row, raw; front row, residual, with additive model main effects removed from both matrices. Each card prints the Spearman r and the number of pairs n.}  % 55 words
\altyazi{fig:estimates_forest}{\textbf{Registered estimates as two hanging tags.} The upper card, Contrasts on panel similarity $\sigma$, holds H1, H2 and descriptive ImageNetV2 rows; the lower card, Directional terms, holds K-b and H3. Circles log, diamonds logit, open marks descriptive; thick and thin bars are 90\% and 95\% intervals, over images only on ImageNetV2. The $\pm$0.10 lines apply to log rows only.}  % 59 words
\altyazi{fig:protocol_settings}{\textbf{Protocol by setting as four exploded boards.} Transfer asymmetry (CNN to ViT minus ViT to CNN) of the ResNet-18 and ViT-Tiny pair: boards 1-4 are the conditioning protocols, set back layer by layer; rows are settings, mean$\pm$SD over three seed pairs with pairs as small circles (SVHN two pairs, no mean). The spine prints the spread over the four protocols.}  % 60 words
\altyazi{fig:protocol_sets}{\textbf{Conditioning sets and measured asymmetry.} Conditioning sets: nested evaluation sets in the CNN-to-ViT direction as terraces (schematic, not area-proportional) with masks and N averaged over seed pairs. Measured asymmetry: mean$\pm$SD of the within-pair difference, pairs as open circles; the steps print the identity term, the marginal subsets both-correct removes and the source robustness successful-source selects on.}  % 56 words
\altyazi{fig:spread_clean_gap}{\textbf{Protocol spread against the clean-accuracy gap on a deep stage.} All 60 model pairs. Back card, Three-protocol spread: unconditioned, target-correct and both-correct, open rings the identity prediction at p = 1; front card, Successful-source minus both-correct: the term the back card leaves out. Markers separate settings; no line is fitted, as pairs share models.}  % 54 words
\altyazi{fig:epsilon_sweep}{\textbf{Robust accuracy under PGD-10 as cut-out profiles.} Each card's top edge traces CIFAR-10 test accuracy over the budget $\eps$, clean to 16/255, as a true vertical length (scale bar 25 points); the number rows print the same values, which carry the result (mean of three seed pairs; WRN-28-10 is one RobustBench model). Depth only orders the models.}  % 57 words
\altyazi{fig:feature_degradation}{\textbf{Feature degradation of ViT-Tiny under attack, block by block.} The clean and PGD-10 image enter the spine, block 1 at the bottom; per block, over three runs: CLS attention entropy change with 90\% TOST intervals inside the $\pm$0.05-nat band, CLS attention displacement (TV), and block-output cosine for three token sets, mean$\pm$SD. The ViT is attacked with its own PGD-10.}  % 59 words
